audit.why: 46.87% over 1788 games. The chart gives Rumble levels 2/3/6 and Yone the two-item stage, and the prose already says the 1v1 is lost by then. That framing is right and I left the difficulty story intact.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 2-3 spike and whys[1] both hang on Soul Unbound being 'on a long cooldown' without ever giving the number, and Fate Sealed is never costed anywhere.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10 seconds — at rank 1 that is a genuinely huge punish window and it shrinks to 10 seconds by rank 5, which is exactly why the lane decays for Rumble as levels go up. Fate Sealed is 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Put 22 seconds at rank 1 on Soul Unbound and 120 seconds on Fate Sealed so both spikes become countable.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup conflates Yone's W and E: wants.foe[0] tells the reader Yone will 'trade his W spirit-form burst'. Spirit form is Soul Unbound (E). W is Spirit Cleave — a cone that shields him, with the shield growing per champion hit. Spirit Cleave is never named or mentioned anywhere, and it is the reason Rumble's chip poke underperforms in this lane. Fate Sealed's actual behaviour (blinks behind the LAST champion in the line and pulls everyone hit toward him) is also never stated.
audit.why: Riot's Spirit Cleave text: 'Cleaves forward, damaging all enemies in a cone. Grants a shield to Yone, the value is increased by the number of champions hit.' Its cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed, so it gets more frequent as he builds. Against Rumble, whose damage is sustained rather than burst, a repeating shield matters more than in most matchups. Fate Sealed: 'Yone blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him' — which makes standing behind your own frontline a positioning error, not a safety measure.
audit.corrected: Name Spirit Cleave and attribute the shield correctly, reserve 'spirit form' for Soul Unbound, and state that Fate Sealed targets the back of the line and drags everyone forward.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (W Spirit Cleave, E Soul Unbound, R Fate Sealed)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Trade on Soul Unbound's cooldown' is the right instruction with no number attached, so a player cannot actually count it.
audit.why: 22 seconds at rank 1 is long enough to run two full Flamespitter rotations; 10 seconds at rank 5 is not. Naming the number is what makes the same sentence useful early and honest late.
audit.corrected: Attach 22 seconds at rank 1 to the trade-on-cooldown rule.

edits.before: Your Q-E-W combo comes fully online — bait his E dash in and walk Flamespitter across his body before Soul Unbound snaps him back.
edits.after: Q-E-W online — Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1, so bait the spirit out and walk Flamespitter across the body it left behind.

edits.before: Dash in with E to get inside Flamespitter's cone, trade his W spirit-form burst, then snap back to safety before you can punish
edits.after: Dash in with Soul Unbound, shield up with Spirit Cleave inside your cone, then snap the spirit back before you can punish

edits.before: Soul Unbound is on a long cooldown at Level 2 and you have Q-E-W online — this is the first real punish window, bait his E dash before committing Flamespitter.
edits.after: Soul Unbound is 22 seconds at rank 1 and you have Q-E-W online — that is the first real punish window, so bait the spirit out before you commit Flamespitter.

edits.before: Short trades are yours at Level 2-3 because Yone must walk into Flamespitter range to do anything — walk the cone across him the moment he steps up, double-Electro-Harpoon if he tries to run, and shield his counter-swing with W. The danger is Soul Unbound: he dashes through you, his spirit does the heavy trading, and he snaps back to where he started — so never commit your full pattern when his E is up and fresh, because you will be the one eating the return damage while he resets. At Level 1 he can Q you safely at the tip of his range and you have no way to punish it cleanly, so stay at the Q-cone edge and accept light chip rather than chasing him into minions and overheating for nothing.
edits.after: Short trades are yours at Level 2-3 because Yone must walk into Flamespitter range to do anything — walk the cone across him as he steps up, double-Electro-Harpoon if he runs, and shield his counter-swing with W. Two things blunt you. Spirit Cleave shields him for more the more champions it clips, so chip poke buys him a buffer instead of a health lead. And Soul Unbound sends his spirit through you to trade before snapping him back — never commit your full pattern while it is up, because you eat the return damage while he resets. It is 22 seconds at rank 1, so count it. At Level 1 he can Mortal Steel you at the tip of its 450 range with no clean punish, so sit at the cone edge and take the chip rather than overheating for nothing.

edits.before: Level 6 is your best window in a different dimension: The Equalizer does not fix the 1v1 but it makes him afraid to roam or fight for Rift Herald because a well-placed wall across the river path is a death sentence for a champion that wants to re-engage with E. In the 1v1, continue to trade on Soul Unbound's cooldown — when it is down he has no escape and you shred him with Danger Zone Flamespitter; when it is up, back off and do not let him trade through the spirit-return burst. Avoid Overheating accidentally here: a silenced Rumble at Level 5 is a free all-in for Yone, who will immediately dash in with E and unload his full combo with zero retaliation available to you.
edits.after: Level 6 is your best window in a different dimension: The Equalizer does not fix the 1v1 but it makes him afraid to roam or fight for Rift Herald, because a well-placed wall across the river path is a death sentence for a champion that wants to re-engage. In the 1v1, keep trading on Soul Unbound’s cooldown — 22 seconds at rank 1, and when it is down he has no escape and you shred him with Danger Zone Flamespitter. Fate Sealed is 120 seconds and blinks behind the LAST champion in its line, dragging everyone hit back toward him, so never be the body behind your own team in a river fight. Avoid Overheating here: a silenced Rumble at Level 5 is a free all-in for Yone, who dashes in and unloads with zero retaliation available to you.

notes: Both packet suspectNames for this matchup are FALSE POSITIVES — 'Use The Equalizer' and "Soul Unbound's" are the correct Riot names. The genuine naming defect the scanner missed is the W/E swap: the page attributed Yone's spirit form to W when W is Spirit Cleave and E is Soul Unbound. Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed, so it speeds up as he itemises — I stated that it shields, not the scaling, because the exact scaling rate is not in the kit file. Rumble's Scrap Shield carries spurious 'knockup' and 'terrain' derived flags; I wrote nothing implying Scrap Shield stops Soul Unbound or Fate Sealed.
